clues.text: This city stands on a wide river in the middle part of its state. Its river port and rail lines helped it grow rich and fast.
clues.narrowing: Rules out edge towns; puts the player at a river port in the middle of its state.

source.quote: The city quickly grew due to its strategic location as a port on the Cumberland River

clues.text: Winters here bring snow most years, but it seldom piles up deep. Summers turn hot and damp, in the style of the upper South.
clues.narrowing: Rules out snowless southern towns; keeps light winter snow with hot damp summers.

source.quote: Snowfall occurs during the winter months, but it is usually not heavy

clues.text: In 1843, this river town was picked as the lasting capital of its state. Three other towns had held the job before, but this one kept it.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to capitals named permanent in 1843 after three earlier seats.

source.quote: In 1843, the city was named as the permanent capital of the state of Tennessee

clues.text: The Grand Ole Opry, a live country music radio show, comes from this city. It is the longest running radio broadcast in the land.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one capital is home to the Grand Ole Opry, the longest running radio broadcast.

source.quote: it is the longest-running radio broadcast in U.S. history

clues.text: The state capitol stands in this city, on a hill. The lawmakers meet in it, and the state governor works here too.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: Tennessee's lawmakers and its governor work in this city, in and around its state capitol.

source.quote: is the capital and most populous city in the U.S. state of Tennessee

reveal.blurb: Founded in 1779 as a river port, Nashville was named the lasting state capital in 1843. Today its country songs earn it the name Music City around the world. The building is the capitol; the city is the capital. Nashville is the capital of Tennessee.
